gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-inria-serif: Commanding yet dignified, Aaargh draws its tubing-like loops with stems and bowls all the same weight. Inria Serif follows with wide-mouthed round letters and diagonals a touch lighter than its verticals, a text serif with real poise.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-joan: Aaargh looks sketched with a pencil that never presses harder. Joan, a text serif with gentle weight shifts and thinner joins where curves meet stems, gives that blunt line a classic editorial partner underneath.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-junge: Authoritative and dignified, Junge is the quiet half of this pairing. Junge keeps its curves generous and thins them only gently, so a long passage would move along smoothly beneath Aaargh's straight-edged, constant strokes.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-kameron: Blunt, tube-like and confident, Aaargh holds its line thickness throughout. And Kameron, a text serif with moderate swelling and curves that refuse to close, feels bookish and editorial beside it, softer where the heading is firm.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-libertinus-serif: Aaargh draws everything with the line weight of a technical drawing pen, bowls and stems alike. And Libertinus Serif, a text serif whose thinnest points still carry real weight, does what the heading can't: handle refined, authoritative running text.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-libre-caslon-text: Aaargh has no pinched joints or flared ends, just constant strokes with a wide-open e. And Libre Caslon Text adds medium-key contrast and unfinished-looking curves, so the page gets a firm voice above a refined one.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-lustria: Hairline-free, shadow-free and blunt. Aaargh is built to command attention, and Lustria, a text serif with a wide-mouthed a and moderate stem-to-hairline ratio, is built to hold a traditional, authoritative tone line after line.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-maitree: Aaargh looks strong and hairline-free, every stroke one steady thickness. Maitree, a text serif, brings open-mouthed curves and a measured swell from hairline to stem, and that pen-like variation is what sets the two apart.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-marcellus: Aaargh glows like neon tubing, every letter drawn with a single steady line thickness and a welcoming e. Shrink it and that glow fades, whereas Marcellus, a classic serif, stays mellow.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-martel: Martel reads easily, with moderate contrast and apertures like a horseshoe magnet. Give that classic serif the larger size and it rewards it, while Aaargh's unshaded, constant strokes carry the heading.
